title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a fabricated depiction of identifiable people presented as a documentary photograph. A real image of three students was altered with AI so that one student was replaced by a different person and the others were reshaped, and the result was published on banners as though it showed an actual Stanford event. The failure is not a model asserting a false fact in text. It is a synthetic image passed off as a record of something that happened, in material the university itself published.

The failure occurred at the production stage, between the original photograph and the finished banner, and it went out without anyone comparing the two. Stanford's own rules already prohibited using AI to create or change images of Stanford people, events, facilities or achievements, and also required disclosure. Catching it would have taken a review step that checked the final asset against the source image and against that policy before publication. The university has said it is adding training and review of materials, which indicates no such check was in place at the time.

What is not established is intent, who performed the edit, and whether anyone faced consequences. The reports describe a university statement confirming the AI use and the policy breach, and a student's account of how he learned of it and how it affected him. A confirmed policy violation is not a finding about why it happened.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology at Stanford, was photographed at a 2024 Lunar New Year party with two other students. Stanford's dining service posted the photo online the next day. When Stanford used the image on banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the other students were altered to look thinner. Ramirez said he learned about it from a friend and found it upsetting.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to change the original image. The university said its rules ban using AI to create or change images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the change and the failure to disclose it broke that policy. Stanford is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to add training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
